content.thinking:
I'm planning the elephant's proportions and coordinate layout, setting a shoulder height around 3.1-3.3 meters with realistic body, tusk, and ear dimensions, and establishing the body's position along the z-axis before building out the full geometry.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, a spine chain running from rump to chest using catmull curve points, and a short neck/head chain attached at the spine's end to orient the head forward and slightly down.

I'm setting up a body sweep path using the hips and spine bones, laying out catmull points from rump through chest to shape the elephant's torso silhouette.

For the barrel-shaped body ellipse I'm thinking through radius and center height -- settling on a centerline around y=2.0 with ry near 1.0 so the top edge lines up near y=3.0, rather than offsetting bones inside the body since they matter less than the surface path itself.

Working out a profile function to taper the body radius smoothly from rump to chest using a sine-based curve...

Still writing shape config...

For skin texture, I'm planning a mottled paint pattern with blended grey tones to give the hide some natural variation.

Now I'm working out the leg structure, planning columnar front legs with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and foot joint positions chained together as a named path for the limb geometry.

For the hind legs, I'm setting hip, knee, hock, and foot positions to create the correct elephant stance, parenting these joints to the hip bone and adjusting the leg radius taper from top to foot before shaping the foot pad geometry.

Adding toe nail details...

Now I'm setting up leg coloring with a gradient that transitions from skin tone near the top to a dusty brown near the base, layering in wrinkle texture for realism.

For the head, I'm sketching out the elephant's skull and forehead using a sweep path with varying radii to form the cranium and dome, planning the joint position and aim direction so the head sits naturally forward and down from the neck.

Now I'm laying out the trunk as a chain of points curving downward and forward from the face, tapering as it descends toward a hanging tip.

Still building the trunk geometry...

Working out the ear geometry...

Writing ear geometry and shading...

Working out the neck and head joint positions, adjusting the spine path so it curves up from the chest through the neck into the cranium, keeping the head sphere centered around y=2.75 without clipping the chest.

Checking proportions against real elephant anatomy, the belly clearance and shoulder height seem roughly right at this scale, so I'm trimming the radius variation to keep the ears from pushing the silhouette too tall.

Now I'm defining the spine bone chain, placing joints along a curve from hips through the shoulders, and setting up the body path as a catmull-rom spline through the hip, mid-spine, and shoulder points.

Then I move on to the neck and head joints, parenting the neck to the last spine joint and the head to the neck, positioning them to extend upward and forward from the shoulders toward the skull.

Shaping the head further with a tapering radius function and faceted sides, then adding a forehead dome and starting on a separate jaw part with its own bone and joint for articulation.

Now I'm placing small dark eye spheres on either side of the head, with amber iris spheres behind them and a flattened brow ridge above, working out the exact coordinates and sizes to keep things proportional to the head's curve.

Now I'm working out the tusk geometry, rooting them near the trunk base and curving the path forward, outward, and slightly upward to about 1.8 meters long, with a tapering radius down to a point at the tip.

I'm shading the ivory tusks with a gradient toward a darker stained tip and adding subtle grain texture, while adjusting the tusk root position outward so it doesn't overlap the trunk.

Plotting the tusk curve points, I'm sizing them so the tip extends slightly past the trunk's end, then adding a small skin-colored collar sphere at the base to blend into the face. Now I'm moving on to building the tail as a chain sprouting from the rump.

But I realize the rump cap's radius pushes the body's back surface further than intended, overlapping with the tail root position—I need to shift the body path's starting z-coordinate to keep the rump from extending too far back.

Working through the proportions, body length should run roughly 3.5-4m from chest to rump, so with rump at z -2.25 and chest front near 1.5, that gives about 3.75, which checks out. Now I'm placing the hind legs under the hip area around z -1.1, with the rump extending behind them to -2.25.

Adjusting the spine and body paths with their control points, setting cap radii and profile shaping so the rump is fuller, and defining the neck curve rising from the body's front point up toward the head. I want the withers hump at the midpoint of the spine to sit slightly higher than the rest of the back, with the overall top of the body around 3.0 and neck/head topping near 3.2 for proper elephant proportions.

Now I'm working out the tail: tracing its path from the root near the rump's rear curve down and back, tapering the radius from thick at the base to thin at the tip, and planning tuft geometry at the tail's end using a ring of card elements angled to simulate hanging hair strands.

Generating spike tuft calls...

Setting up the forehead bristle scatter with dark tapered-triangle textures tinted rather than drawn grey. Beyond that I'm thinking through surface details like knee wrinkles, tusks, ear veins, trunk rings, tail tuft, and skin mottling, mostly handling these through paint layers rather than extra geometry.

Now I'm layering the body paint itself: countershading over a mottled base with a lighter belly and dust gradient, then nesting subtle flank wrinkle stripes at an angled axis with a muted brownish-grey tone on top of that combined texture.

Then I settle on the final palette—muddy skin, darker shadow tone, lighter belly, and a pinkish inner-ear hue—and start adding small anatomical bumps like shoulder blade spheres to add sculptural detail to the body.

For the legs, I'm shaping the taper by assigning a radius profile along the limb—thicker at the top, narrower at the knee, then flaring slightly at the ankle like a real elephant leg.

Checking shoulder joint placement against the body width, I'm nudging the leg's x-position inward so it doesn't poke outside the torso silhouette, then laying out the front leg path with four control points running from shoulder down to foot.

Still defining foot pad geometry...

Flaring outer nails outward with symmetric positions, four front nails and three hind nails slightly embedded into the pad at radius 0.36. Working out the hind leg path with knee shifted forward, naming the joints hipL, kneeL, hockL, footH for parenting.

Still defining joint naming... adding jaw joint and geometry, then moving on to cheek and temporal details.

Plotting the trunk's downward curve with tapering radii from base to tip, keeping the tip above the floor so the sweep caps cleanly without clipping.

Now I'm writing a paint function for the trunk that blends skin and dark tones into rings based on position along the trunk, using a sine-based modulation for the striping effect and making sure unused parameters are properly prefixed to avoid lint errors.

For the rest of the body, I'm reusing the trunk's striped paint for legs via a gradient wrapper, skipping mouth details, and applying the head's countershaded coat paint to the neck and head for consistent mottling and wrinkles. Then I'm adding scattered bristle cards to the forehead using a surface scatter with distance and normal-based filtering, rendering each tuft as a small SVG shape.

Now I'm sketching a tuft card shape in white and setting its sizing, lean angle, and dark brown color for texture detail, while considering whether to add similar cards along the tail spikes. For extra surface richness I'm weighing adding small torus rings at the knees to suggest wrinkle folds, rotating them horizontally to sit naturally around the leg geometry.

Adding wrist and elbow torus rings...

I verify the normal checks out, then adjust the ear angle to flare outward around 27-45° from the back axis, settling on a direction vector near (0.65,0,-0.76). I double check the ear's reach — extending roughly 0.45 back over the shoulder and out to about x=1.25 — which looks right against the reference.

I make a slight tilt adjustment for the ear's y-axis to flare outward, confirm the head width and position with the ear attached around x=0.42, then verify nothing floats above the floor — ear tops sit near 3.45, feet rest at 0, so the proportions hold together.

Now I'm setting up the metadata export with name, description, style, and commit hash, and defining the color palette constants for skin, dark accents, belly, pink, ivory, nails, eyes, and hair. I'm also considering TypeScript typing concerns around radius arrays and tuple inference when a function returns a coordinate pair.

Writing elephant builder joints...

Setting the tail chain's role and parent to hips, then adding a ring of hair spikes around the tail using b.ring and b.spike, checking that the tilt option correctly leans each spike toward the line's direction.

Adding a central tuft spike at the tail tip, aligned with its tangent direction. For the nails, I'm using parts attached to a rigid bone at the foot tip, and skipping the pupil's direction handling. I'm also adding nostril discs as cylinders positioned at the trunk tip's frame.
